summary.text: A 14-year-old male presented to the ophthalmology outpatient department with severe bilateral visual impairment, particularly under bright light. Slit-lamp examination showed a clear anterior chamber, a cataractous lens nucleus and characteristic powdery opacities, leading to a diagnosis of bilateral cataracta pulverulenta without ectopia lentis.

Systemic examination showed features suggestive of a connective tissue disorder: long arm span with a ratio of 1.35, high-arched palate, nasal voice, arachnodactyly and pectus excavatum. Echocardiography showed a small 9 mm atrial septal defect with trace tricuspid and mitral regurgitation. The revised Ghent systemic score exceeded 7, confirming Marfan syndrome.

The patient underwent manual small incision cataract surgery under peribulbar anesthesia after full pharmacologic pupil dilation, with scleral tunnel creation, capsulorhexis, hydrodissection, nucleus extraction, cortical aspiration and posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation, and received subconjunctival gentamicin and dexamethasone. Postoperative best-corrected visual acuity was 6/6.
